latest_posts.caption:
we can fix the future of marketing, but we need your help !!!!

so much of what gets written about the future of marketing is guesswork, with big predictions made by people who never stopped to ask the marketers doing the work, and we’ve never wanted PLM to work like that. everything we’ve built since 2020 has come from listening to you, from the posts that sparked the biggest conversations to the events and community you asked us for

so before anyone decides what the future looks like, we want to hear it from you. 

PLM x you is our big survey for marketers and it is your chance to tell us what’s on your mind right now, what you’re finding hard, what you want to learn and what you’d love to see more of from us

it takes around 5 minutes to complete, your answers will shape the future of what we do next. comment HERO for the link (or find it in our bio if ya don’t fancy leaving a note below)

love, team PLM ⋆.˚ ☾⭒.˚

brands are winning by giving away the one thing money can’t: access 💸₊˚⊹💲 ♡

the brands people stick with aren’t just selling a product, they’re letting you in before the decision is made: a first look, a say in what gets built, watching the thing happen instead of seeing the polished version after.

we learned from the people behind the brands doing this best: @georginahoneyman, senior social media manager at @adanola, on treating their broadcast channel as real access, and MacKenzie Kassab on how @rarebeauty’s newsletter showed the proof behind the campaign.

plus how @refybeautylet their community shape skin base, and how @goodgirlsnacks built in public before they had a product to sell.

which brands do you think do this well? drop them below, we’d love to hear your picks !!

POV: you spent the day at our first ever conference (pinch us !!!!) and this is what you saw (spoiler: it was awesome) 🤭⭐️✨🎤💫📸

first up, George told us 90% of your audience isn’t ready to buy yet, so stop selling and start giving !!!!

then beyond the brand account, where the panel debated whether humanising a brand had to mean a face, and whether founder-led really worked 👀 

Grace’s take: it takes a cast, not one founder, but a group of faces that each has a different job. what’s realistic for you? and who can make up your cast?

then Ray showed us social is a search engine now. discovery has changed, so posting and hoping doesn’t work anymore. good social SEO means knowing the problems your audience is trying to solve and the words they actually use, because keywords alone won’t cut it 🤘

our speakers got all the claps !!!!

Faye and Sophie had a live and candid chat on on how to build a presence people care about when you’re the strategy and the execution, from joining culture instead of creating it, to why people buy from people, to the litmus test of would you stop on your own for you page (complete with matching tees, so iconic) 

then the trust panel got into whether leaders are wrong to still want follower report 🤫 

Lucy’s take: they’re not, you just have to start from your goal, not your metric. if you’re selling a pan, trust isn’t the thing to track, quality and durability is, so work out the few things people really care about and measure against those!

and Verity made the case for a new metric: brand love - which is a long game, not influencer marketing with a new name, and the way you get leadership to back it is to tie it to the numbers a CFO cares about: retention, LTV and conversion 🤓 

and chloe closed on how to survive the scroll, encouraging us that it’s okay to spend guilt-free time online and teaching us how to recognise the signs of burnout when you’re professionally online 🧠

the girls are starting group accounts, and they’re growing faster than most solo creators ever manage 👀 

@4inthe5 post their lives across New York, @thefashionfourcast drop a new outfit episode every Saturday and @eri.gyalz travel as a collective. 

each one has a handful of friends behind a single handle, and the feeds run like your favourite tv show (!!)

let’s chat below: do you think group accounts will be the next big format, is short-form just late to the trend or the format just another fleeting moment?

the team behind @transportforlondon have what might be the hardest social job in London: making a transport network of millions feel human, under governance where the margin for error is close to nothing ｡°🚂༄｡° ⋆·˚ ༘ * 

most brands with that much to lose play it safe and post nothing. this feed does the opposite, and they’ve built a whole process for getting fun ideas signed off without losing the plot.

swipe for how they do it !!

🔗 the full interview drops September 22nd for our email readers only, so comment MINDTHEGAP and I’ll send you the free sign up link

I went to @shop.ltk’s LTKCon in Texas on a press pass and spent three days with the highest earning creators in the world 👀✨

I wrote all of it up in this month’s deep dive. comment DIVE and I’ll send you the link !!

@mackenziekassab, the woman behind the @rarebeauty Secrets Substack on how they’re winning by doing the one thing most brands can’t bring themselves to do... which is nothing 👀

swipe for the full breakdown and let me know below, what brands do you love on Substack? have you tried it yourself? and is it a platform you’re looking to try?

Jessica landed a role she didn’t even apply for, and Tameka works with brands alongside her full-time job. Jerrica and the Creator Match team paid out over $1,000,000 to LinkedIn Creators in a single year (!!!!)
